title: Veredictum performance result
description: One performance run against one server: the `raw` evidence (the target's System OPTIONS answer, the environment, the generator, the embedded workload and corpus, the seed, the scout windows and per plateau the encoded HDR histograms per hold half and operation) and the `derived` numbers, which `veredictum perf-judge` recomputes from `raw` byte for byte. Percentiles come from summed histograms, never an average of percentiles. No openEHR specification governs performance; this is the instrument's own design.

options.description: The answer to ITS-REST System OPTIONS (specifications/operations/options.yaml), or the transport failure that prevented one.
The members of the `Options` document the server sent; a member the schema does not name is not carried.

restapi_specs_version.description: The ITS-REST release the server states it implements.

conformance_profile.description: The conformance profile the server states.

reason.description: Why the body is not an `Options` document, in the parser's own words.

status.description: A three-digit code outside 100..599, which RFC 9110 §15 makes invalid.

posture.description: What was switched on behind these numbers. A run declares exactly one named posture profile out of the set its pack defines, and black-box canaries bracket the measured window: every item is labelled `verified` when both brackets observed the declared value first-hand, and `declared-only` when nothing on the wire discloses it. A canary that contradicted the declaration, or a pair of brackets that disagreed, refused the run, so no such record exists.

comparability.description: Every item on which the measured deployment's own configuration departs from the profile named above. A same-machine baseline is composed from somebody else's pinned recipe, so where that recipe configures an item differently the run declares, and the canaries check, what the deployment actually does; this block is how the record says so. Absent for a run that declared its profile as the pack defines it.

recipe_sha256.description: The digest of the recipe the corpus was seeded from.

compositions.description: The compositions the server held when the clock started, as read back.

seeding.description: The seeding before the clock, a closed-loop bulk load reported apart from every measured number.

operations_per_interaction.description: Planned rates count operation arrivals per second; the generator draws interactions at the rate divided by this.

multiple.description: The planned rate as a multiple of the scout's knee estimate.

server.description: The server-side readings over the hold: context that never bears on qualification. Each is present, or absent with its reason.

containers.description: The declared containers' cumulative counters from the Docker Engine API stats endpoint, read at a fixed interval from the hold's start and once at its end. A failed reading ends that container's series, with the reason.

database.description: The database's pg_database_size and per-schema pg_total_relation_size at the hold's start and end.

statements.description: The statements pg_stat_statements counted over the hold, by execution and planning time, costliest first.

between_run_noise.description: One pass measures sampling intervals only; between-run noise needs an interleaved A/A comparison.

scope.const: A run of at most ten minutes measures steady-state capacity and says nothing about memory growth, data growth or behaviour over hours.

knee.description: The highest offered rate whose plateau and every lower one qualify: a bracket up to the first failing plateau, a lower bound when the top plateau qualifies, or below the ladder when the lowest fails.

peak.description: The highest achieved throughput of the run, whatever its latency.

usl.description: The Universal Scalability Law X(N) = γN / (1 + α(N − 1) + βN(N − 1)) fitted to achieved throughput against mean in flight over the scout windows and the plateaus: an explanatory model, never a verdict. The fit is pinned arithmetic, so `perf-judge` reproduces it.

population.description: The population the knee could serve at its peak: the knee divided by 13 to 75 peak API arrivals per second per 100,000 population, read at the run's corpus scale and environment.

derivation.const: About 46 clinical documents per capita per year (consultations, discharges and ED visits from OECD Health at a Glance 2023 and Eurostat; laboratory results from RCPath; imaging from the NHS Diagnostic Imaging Dataset 2023/24; prescription items from NHS BSA PCA 2024/25) give 0.15 writes per second per 100,000 population; a peak factor of 8 (the ITU-T E.500 busy hour) and a read multiplier of 10:1 to 50:1 (OLTP-Bench and YCSB; PMC10148376) give 13 to 75 peak API arrivals per second per 100,000. The knee divided by that band is the population a deployment of this shape could serve at its peak, read only at the corpus scale and on the environment the run used.

scout_estimate.description: K̂, the knee estimate the ladder's rates are multiples of: the midpoint rate of the first breaching scout window, or the ramp's end rate as a lower bound when no window breached.

mean_in_flight.description: Little's law: the rate of the timed exchanges times their mean latency.
